name: The Paintings Everyone Knows, and the Stories Behind Them
description: The Mona Lisa, the Starry Night and a few dozen other works that nearly every visitor to a museum wants to see, with the stories of who made them and why they last.

checkpoints.name: The Renaissance
checkpoints.note: Artists in Florence, Rome and the Low Countries learn perspective and anatomy, and paint the faces and scenes that museums still draw crowds with.

checkpoints.name: Courts and Golden Ages
checkpoints.note: Spanish kings and Dutch merchants hire painters who catch light, character and daily life, and put the viewer inside the picture.

checkpoints.name: Romantic revolutions
checkpoints.note: Painters turn to politics, disaster and nature, while Japanese woodblock prints reach Europe and change how artists see.

checkpoints.name: The modern eye
checkpoints.note: Impressionists, Post-Impressionists and their followers paint light and feeling, and nervous or golden images become icons.

checkpoints.name: Isms and icons
checkpoints.note: Cubism, Surrealism, protest and Pop turn paintings into statements, and a painted soup can sits beside an old master in the museum.
